rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra completes the preceding Sūrat al-Najm by explaining the Hour's certainty and nearness, and the differing outcomes of those guided by revelation and those led by desire.
rows.anchor: بيان آخر النجم في أمر الساعة من تحققها وشدة قربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's confirming signs establish God's power to create and annihilate and His exclusive sovereignty; the moon's nighttime effect signals the Hour's approach and God's power to overturn the heavens.
rows.anchor: وعد بذلك بإخبار نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم وتحقق صدقه بما أيده به من آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is named al-Qamar because the moon carries the sign of nearness foreshadowed by al-Najm; al-Inshiqāq was avoided because an unqualified splitting title would more properly suggest the sky.
rows.anchor: فلذلك سميت بما تضمنته من الاقتراب المنجم به النجم بالإشارة لا بالعبارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God's encompassing knowledge and complete power, mercy extending to both wretched and felicitous, and perfected blessing for those He chooses.
rows.anchor: الرحمن } الذي وسعت رحمته كل شيء فعمت الشقي والسعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening echoes al-Najm's closing threat that the denied Resurrection is near, while extending the preceding sūra's celestial signs from stars to the moon.
rows.anchor: لما ختمت النجم بالتهديد باقتراب القيامة التي ينكرونها بعد أن فتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is drawing very close, the moment when Resurrection occurs; little time remains relative to history since Adam because the final Prophet has come and no later community is awaited.
rows.anchor: اللحظة التي لا ساعة في الحقيقة غيرها التي تقوم فيها القيامة لأنه قل ما بقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form of the verb is itself a sign of God's immense power over the Hour.
rows.anchor: دالا على عظيم اقتداره عليها بتأنيث فعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The swift, effortless rupture of the moon is a warning sign whose extraordinary celestial effect demonstrates God's power over the coming Hour and calls people to prepare.
rows.anchor: وكانت الآيات السماوية أعظم , فاتأثير فيها أدل على تمام الاقتدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs know the lunar signs that regulate their livelihood; disrupting a celestial cause of worldly life demonstrates God's power to alter the heavenly bodies and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب أعرف الناس بها , دلهم على التأثير فيه على اقترابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's splitting was a real, famous event in the Prophet's lifetime, supported by the Qur'an and the accepted reports that make it nearly mass-transmitted.
rows.anchor: وانشقاق القمر على حقيقيته في زمان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر شهير جدا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says exegetes unanimously affirm the historical splitting and cites Ibn Masʿūd's report, with no dissent from him.
rows.anchor: وإجماع أهل التفسير عليه كما قاله القشيري

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأنس
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Anas report in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections that Quraysh requested a sign and the Prophet showed the moon split, with one part on either side of Ḥirāʾ; al-Biqāʿī calls the report nearly mass-transmitted.
rows.anchor: رواه الشيخان عن ابن مسعود وأنس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī gives the occasion of revelation: Quraysh's polytheists told the Prophet to split the moon if he was truthful.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : سبب نزولها أن مشركي العرب من قريش قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن كنت صادقا فشق

rows.speaker: من قال المراد به سيشق
rows.claim: The future reading that the moon will split is rejected because there is no contextual indicator to move the past tense into the future, especially given the famous sound report.
rows.anchor: ومن قال : المراد به ( سيشق ) يحتاج في صرف الماضي عن حقيقته إلى المستقبل إلى صارف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the opening to the preceding account of the final return and Resurrection: the Hour is near so that those able to heed may desist.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما أعلمهم سبحانه بأن إليه المنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī traces a continuing denunciation of polytheism and resistance to revelation from al-Zumar through Ghāfir and Fuṣṣilat, showing the context of al-Qamar's warning.
rows.anchor: ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of later sūras keeps reproaching deniers through warnings about shirk, rejecting the Qur'an, disputing God's signs, and the fate awaiting disbelievers.
rows.anchor: كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه والذين يحاجون في الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatḥ's promise of victory presses the disbelievers more than reproach, while al-Ḥujurāt honors the Prophet and unites believers in ways that frustrate the envious enemy.
rows.anchor: وأما سورة الفتح فما تضمنته من البشارة والفتح أشد على الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Dhāriyāt, al-Ṭūr, and al-Najm make the preceding theme especially clear, announcing it in their openings.
rows.anchor: وأما سورة الذاريات والطور والنجم فما تضمنته مما ذكرناه قبل أوضح شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After earlier peoples' denials and destruction, al-Qamar turns directly to the Meccan polytheists: they are no different from those peoples and should not mistake God's forbearance for safety; its opening and ending frame this admonition.
rows.anchor: ولم يحيروا جوابا فيما عرض عليهم سبحانه في سورة القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra recounts each nation's denial and destruction with concise, forceful expression, ending each story with the recurring question about God's punishment and warnings.
rows.anchor: فذكر سبحانه لهم قصة كل أمة وهلاكها عند تكذيبها بأعظم إيجاز وأجزل إيراد

words: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated refrain says the Qur'an is accessible for remembrance, removing the excuse that its warnings and lessons are too difficult to understand.
rows.anchor: ولقد سيرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers need to accept all revelation and act on its clear rulings; deeper understanding of difficult and ambiguous matters is a gift God grants to people He elevates in knowledge.
rows.anchor: يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated accounts of prophets and their peoples across several sūras provide sufficient lessons, while combining them yields a straight path and manifest light.
rows.anchor: تكرار قصص الأنبياء مع أممهم في عدة سور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question comparing Meccan disbelievers to earlier peoples echoes Shuʿayb's warning not to let hostility bring the fate of earlier nations upon his people.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه عواقب الأمم في تكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Quraysh's united force would prevail is answered by the prediction of their defeat at Badr and the killing of their chiefs, leaving them no argument.
rows.anchor: إي إنكم تعلقتم بتألفكم وجماعتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qamar's stories show that deniers were seized and destroyed, then turn to address the Arabs directly; unlike the extensive accounts in al-Aʿrāf and Hūd, they complete the purpose of warning Quraysh.
rows.anchor: إنما مساق القصص في هذه السورة واعتماد التعريف بحال من ذكر في أن كذبوا وعاندوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Aʿrāf, Hūd, al-Muʾminūn, and al-Shuʿarāʾ, narrative admonition begins with gentleness and indirect warning, growing harsher only after repeated calls fail; al-Qamar's direct rebuke of Quraysh completes the shift.
rows.anchor: وذلك غير خاف في التلطف بالموعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shuʿarāʾ explicitly rebukes the polytheists, clears the Prophet of their false accusations, and ends by warning wrongdoers of their fate.
rows.anchor: فوبخهم وعنفهم ونزه نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم عن توهمهم وعظيم إفكهم وافترائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Shuʿarāʾ, the refrain that each narrated episode contains a sign carries threat and warning, reinforcing the sūra's direct reproof.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك } وفيه تهديد ووعيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Although al-insān is a generic noun, Adam is its foremost referent here; Ibn ʿAbbās's view that Adam is intended does not exclude the human species generally.
rows.anchor: - كما قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما - لا تمنع إرادة الجنس من حيث هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayān is the human rational and speaking faculty: it grasps particulars and universals, infers absent matters from present ones by signs or calculation, distinguishes good from evil, and communicates thought through speech, action, writing, and gesture.
rows.anchor: وهي الإدراك للأأمور الكلية والجزئية والحكم الحاضر والغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This faculty enables people to perfect themselves and teach others, making bayān the means for learning the Qur'an; its familiarity to humans should not obscure its extraordinary divine gift, displayed in Adam's knowledge before the angels.
rows.anchor: فصار بذلك ذا قدرة على الكمال في نفسه والتكميل لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets ḥusbān as the calculated courses of the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: بحسبان * } أي جريهما , يجري كل منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon's precise courses mark all units of time and order earthly affairs; their stable regularity proves a sustaining, alert Creator, while their eventual undoing and varying day-night cycles show His free agency.
rows.anchor: وهذا على تطاول الأويام والدهور لا يختل ذرة دلالة

words: يرسل عليكما شواظ من نار ونحاس
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat to block escape from the heavens shows that all human power depends on God; he sends this sign to break the hard-hearted person's assumption that inability is merely unfamiliarity rather than God's restraint.
rows.anchor: ولما سلب عنهم القدرة على النفوذ المذكور تنبيها على سلب جميع القدرة عنهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the address to mean the people emerging from their graves as they are driven to the gathering place.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : حين تخرجون من القبور بسوقكم إلى المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shawāẓ is a massive, spreading, constricted flame that surrounds them and makes a loud sound.
rows.anchor: لهب عظيم منتشر مع التضايق محيط بكم من كل جانب له صوت شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word shawāẓ can also mean a smokeless flame, smoke and heat of fire, or other related phenomena.
rows.anchor: الشواظ يطلق على اللهب الذي لا دخان فيه وعلى دخان النار وحرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the nuḥās as terrifying smoke with flying sparks and molten material.
rows.anchor: دخان هو في غاية الفظاعة فيه شرر متطاير وقطر مذاب

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr says Arabs call smoke nuḥās, pronouncing its nūn with either ḍamma or kasra.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير : والعرب تسمي الدخان نحاسا بضم النون وكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers use ḍamma on the nūn; Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read it with kasra as a genitive coordinate to nār, while the others use nominative coordination with shawāẓ.
rows.anchor: وأجمع القراء على ضمها - انتهى . وجرها أبو عمرو وابن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inability to save themselves follows because, although such a trap is possible by reason and custom, they know from experience that no one caught in it could escape.
rows.anchor: وكانوا عارفين بأنهم لو وقعوا في مثل ذلك لم يتخلصوا منه بوجه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Burjān presents the threat as fulfilling the Prophet's report that a neck of fire will call every arrogant tyrant, pluck them from the crowd like a pigeon picking sesame, and cover criminals with smoke that does not harm believers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : هذا مصداق قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is itself a favor because it offers correction and delays punishment; the repeated question asks whether they deny the gift of hearing or other blessings despite worldly signs that should lead them to faith.
rows.anchor: فهو نعمة عليهم والعفو عن المعالجة
